⚠ Stop using this appliance
Water near the plug or socket is dangerous. Please don't touch the plug, socket or machine if they or your hands are wet. If you can do it safely, switch off the circuit at the consumer unit (fuse box), keep away from the water, and don't use the machine again until a qualified electrician or appliance engineer has checked it. This sounds serious because water is near your plug sockets, which creates a significant risk of electric shock or short-circuiting. Do not touch any wet plugs or switches with wet hands. Once you have isolated the power, please check if there is standing water inside the bottom of the machine (under the filter). Is there water in the base?

i havent turned the power off yet, its still running!! the water is spreading toward an extension lead on the floor. do i just switch off the fuse box? i havent opened the door properly yet, its full of bubbles

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Yes, switch off the circuit at your consumer unit (fuse box) immediately. Do not touch the plug or extension lead while they are wet or near water. Once the power is definitely off, you can safely open the door and check for standing water in the base.
ok switching it off at the fuse box now. the machine was still running when i messaged and theres loads of suds, housemate squirted fairy washing up liquid in cos we ran out of tablets. is that why??

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Yes, that is exactly why. Fairy (or any hand-washing liquid) creates massive amounts of foam in a dishwasher because there isn't enough water to dilute it properly. This foam expands and pushes its way out past the door seal, which explains the mess on your floor. Once we know that, I can guide you through clearing the suds safely. However, because the water has reached your plug sockets and extension lead, please do not use the appliance again until a qualified engineer has inspected it for safety.
